items.title: Pug Horton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: I acknowledged Connie Haines and Louise Tobin out in the audience, and I sang a song for them

ctx.x: Well the greats certainly knew that, Ellington and so on.

You see all those wonderful gestures as the musicians in the brass section and the way they would throw up their horns, and the guys moving, I mean it was wonderful and it was not playing down to the audience in any way, it was a sense of joy. I just love it. I love to bring people in. I think it’s fantastic. And it’s amazing, when we did this performance we did something and I acknowledged Connie Haines and Louise Tobin out in the audience, and I sang a song for them, I sang Billy Strayhorn’s “A Flower is a…
Over the years, did you ever run into any racial — I don’t know exactly what the word would be—
